start.text: A stone bench, worn hollow down the middle by nine hundred years of somebody lying on it. The blanket at its head is folded the way the Quiet House folds them: in three, and the edge turned under.
You put your hand in the hollow. It's cold. Of course it is. Whoever lay here last lay here last midwinter, and was ready, and was given.
And then, three months ago, nobody came down for the next three. They stayed in the Quiet House, full, humming.
